parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour commits to achieving clean power by 2030 as a core mission, establishing a publicly owned Great British Energy company capitalised at £8.3 billion, ending new oil and gas field licences, banning fracking, and investing in home insulation and renewables while managing existing North Sea fields responsibly.

citations.quote: To drive forward investment in clean, next parliament. home-grown energy production, Labour will create a new publicly- owned company, Great British
We will not issue new licences to explore new fields because they will not take a penny off bills, cannot make us energy secure, and will only accelerate the worsening climate crisis.

results.headline: Labour pledges clean energy superpower status by 2030
results.quote: Make Britain a clean energy superpower to cut bills, create jobs and deliver security with cheaper, zero-carbon electricity by 2030, accelerating to net zero.

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservatives commit to delivering net zero by 2050 via a pragmatic approach, trebling offshore wind capacity, expanding nuclear power including Small Modular Reactors, legislating for annual North Sea licensing rounds, and reducing green levies on household bills while rejecting Labour's 2030 clean power target as unaffordable.

citations.quote: We are proud of our record and remain committed to delivering net zero by 2050. Today the UK is home to the five largest offshore wind farms in the world.
citations.source: Conservative and Unionist Party Manifesto 2024, p.48

citations.quote: Within the first 100 days of the next Parliament, we will approve two new fleets of Small Modular Reactors to rapidly expand nuclear power, create well-paid, high-skilled jobs and deliver cheaper, cleaner and more secure energy.
citations.source: Conservative and Unionist Party Manifesto 2024, p.49

results.headline: Conservatives promise affordable transition to sustainable energy
results.quote: Delivering an affordable transition to domestic, sustainable energy.

results.headline: Conservative MP: decarbonise affordably without harming communities
results.quote: We believe in decarbonisation, but we need to do it in a way that people can afford and that does not trash our country in the process.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrats pledge to achieve net zero by 2045, pursue a 68% emissions reduction by 2030, launch an emergency home energy upgrade programme, remove restrictions on solar and wind, implement a windfall tax on oil and gas super-profits, and restore the UK's global leadership role on climate.

citations.quote: Liberal Democrats are committed to cutting greenhouse gas emissions to net zero by 2045 at the latest.
Helping people with the cost of living and their energy bills by implementing a proper, one-off windfall tax on the super-profits of oil and gas producers and traders.

results.headline: Lib Dems commit to net zero by 2045
results.quote: Take the action needed now to achieve net zero by 2045.

results.headline: Lib Dem peer: cost of oil crisis exceeds cost of net zero
results.quote: The Climate Change Committee was clear last week that the cost of another oil price crisis would be greater than the cost of reaching net zero by 2050, so these Benches fully support the need to roll out renewables at a faster rate.

parties.name: Plaid Cymru
parties.summary: Plaid Cymru advocates for full Welsh control over energy powers and natural resources, establishing a community energy company Ynni Cymru, opposing new nuclear stations and oil and gas licences, maintaining the fracking ban, and creating a Welsh Green New Deal to transition workers into green jobs.

citations.quote: Plaid Cymru has long made the case for the establishment of our own national energy company, Ynni Cymru, which we succeeded in establishing through working with the Welsh Government.

We will create a Welsh Green New Deal. This will create rewarding, meaningful and fair work in the emerging green and net-zero sector, and includes re-skilling and supporting Welsh employees and apprentices into these sectors

results.headline: Plaid Cymru commits to net zero in Wales by 2035 and reversing biodiversity decline by 2030
results.quote: Plaid Cymru recognises that the climate and nature emergencies are the biggest threat to mankind on a global scale, and reaffirms our commitment to reaching net-zero targets in Wales by 2035 and reversing biodiversity decline by 2030.
